To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Learning case-based planning knowledge is a difficult task, and 2. Learning case-based knowledge sources interact with one another, and the interactions are important to the learning process.

the learning processes that improve the performance of a case-based planner are those that: (1) improve the quality of case-based reasoning; (2) do so at low cost; and (3) do not interfere with each other.

the interactions between different learning methods are important and that a promising method for combining different learning methods is to use the output of each method as a feature in a learning method that combines all methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of integrating multiple learning processes for case-based planning and reasoning.
the problem of how to integrate multiple learning processes in a case-based reasoning (CBR) system, and how to evaluate the utility of different integration methods.
how to learn from multiple sources in case-based reasoning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
learning to integrate multiple knowledge sources is an important and useful approach that can improve the performance of case based reasoning systems.
the integration of multiple learning methods is an important factor in improving case-based reasoning.
the results of the case study are promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the integration of learning methods can significantly improve the performance of case-based reasoning, and the benefits of integration can be realized without a significant increase in the computational complexity of the overall system.
we can learn a lot from the case-based reasoning process.
the combination of learning mechanisms is a very promising direction for improving case-based reasoning.

learning is a crucial part of CBR, and it is important to understand the interactions between different learning mechanisms.
learning to learn can be an effective way of improving case-based reasoning.
